alt: Two Dyson CameraJet electric toothbrushes in Ceramic Ultra Blue standing next to a bathroom sink, showing the compact design with an AI camera module mounted beneath the brush head
story: Dyson launched the CameraJet on September 1, 2026 — a $499 electric toothbrush with a 100,000-pixel AI camera that fires precision mouthrinse jets at detected plaque gaps, backed by 16 million lines of code, 470,000 dental training images, and a team of fluid dynamicists — to automate what dental floss does for about $3.
why_funny: Dyson recruited ML engineers, fluid dynamicists, and Singapore's National University to build a product whose core value proposition is 'we noticed you weren't flossing and decided the answer was a camera in your mouth.'
